papers.title_in_file: Solving General QUBOs with Warm-Start QAOA via a Reduction to Max-Cut
papers.version_note: arXiv:2504.06253v2, 22 Sep 2025; the ACM Trans. Quantum Comput. format. The text layer printed the word convex as QUBO-Relaxed in many places and lost most mathematical symbols.
papers.what_it_is: An empirical study of warm-start QAOA for general QUBOs via a reduction to Max-Cut with SDP warm-starts (GW, BM), compared with the QUBO-relaxation warm-start on random, TSP, portfolio and MIS instances of 16 variables.

existing.value: The authors state that the performance of QUBO-Relaxed is strongly dependent on the number of random initial conditions tested.
quotes: Because QUBO-Relaxed relies on a non-QUBO-Relaxed optimization problem, its performance is strongly dependent on the number of random initial conditions tested by the optimizer.
existing.note: Right as stored. The paper also reports an empirical 10 versus 50 initialization comparison (Sec. 4.1): 50 slightly outperformed 10 in general, problem dependent.

existing.value: The authors state they compare the two warm-start approaches for a variety of QUBO types up to 16 variables.
quotes: We empirically compare the two warm-start approaches above for a variety of different types of QUBOs up to 16 variables.
existing.certainty_reason: The paper's own scope statement in Section 1, repeated in Section 3.3.
existing.note: Right as stored; Sec. 3.3 repeats it (each problem is a QUBO in 16 variables).

existing.value: The authors find that the best choice of warm-start approach is strongly dependent on the problem type.
quotes: We find that the best choice of warmstart approach is strongly dependent on the problem type.
existing.note: Right as stored; Sec. 1 adds that the best approach also depends on the metric of success, and Sec. 5 says the relative performance is problem and metric dependent.

assertions.value: The authors state that this work applies the semidefinite warm-starts to a broader class of problem instances by using a standard reduction that transforms any QUBO instance into a Max-Cut instance.
quotes: This work leverages these semidefinite warmstarts for a broader class of problem instances by using a standard reduction that transforms any QUBO instance into a Max-Cut instance.

assertions.value: The authors state that the QUBO to Max-Cut mapping introduces an additional auxiliary qubit or variable, and that a derivation of the mapping is in Appendix A.
quotes: This “QUBO to Max-Cut” mapping introduces an additional auxiliary qubit/variable.
A derivation of this mapping can be found in Appendix A.
assertions.certainty_reason: The mapping is defined in Section 2.1.1 and derived in Appendix A.

assertions.value: The authors report that, when mapping a QUBO to a Max-Cut instance, the auxiliary qubit is frequently the best choice of qubit for the vertex-at-top heuristic.
quotes: Interestingly, when mapping a QUBO to a Max-Cut instance, we find that the auxiliary qubit is frequently the best choice of qubit for the vertex-at-top heuristic

assertions.value: The authors state, citing [9], that solving the QUBO relaxation is known to be NP-Hard for general QUBOs.
quotes: for general QUBOs, solving this relaxation is known to be NP-Hard [9]

assertions.value: The authors report that they benchmarked random QUBOs, the traveling salesman problem, portfolio optimization and maximum independent set, the last on Erdős–Rényi and Newman–Watts–Strogatz graphs.
quotes: We benchmarked this approach on various QUBO problems: Random QUBOs, TSP, Portfolio Optimization, and MIS.
We study this problem on two different graph ensembles, the Erdős–Rényi (GNP) model and the Newmann-Watts-Strogatz (NWS) model.

assertions.value: The authors report that each problem is a QUBO in 16 variables with a 17-vertex corresponding graph, that 1000 instances were generated and run at depth zero, and that 10 of those 1000 were run at higher depths.
quotes: For all of the following problems, 1000 instances were generated and ran at depth
10 of those 1000 were selected to be run at depths
Each problem is a QUBO in 16 variables with a corresponding 17-vertex corresponding graph.

assertions.value: The authors define two performance metrics: an instance-specific approximation ratio inspired by the cut ratio, and the optimal sampling probability.
quotes: The first is inspired by the cut ratio
The second is the optimal sampling probability,

assertions.value: The authors report that QAOA parameters were optimized using COBYLA and that all simulations used a custom QAOA simulator.
quotes: The parameters were optimized using COBYLA.
All simulations were computed with a custom QAOA simulator based on [35].

assertions.value: The authors report that GW2 was selected as the representative warmstart because its instance-specific approximation ratios and optimal sampling probabilities were comparable to or better than the other warmstarts considered.
quotes: GW2 was selected as the representative warmstart because it obtained instancespecific approximation ratios and optimal sampling probabilities which were either comparable to or better than the other warmstarts considered.

assertions.value: The authors report that BM2 and BM3 obtain approximation ratios comparable to the GW warmstarts but significantly lower optimal sampling probabilities.
quotes: While both BM2 and BM3 perform comparable to the GW warmstarts in terms of their obtained instancespecific approximation ratio, they obtain significantly lower optimal sampling probabilities.

assertions.value: The authors state that the lower BM optimal sampling probabilities are likely due to the warmstarts finding relatively high cost solutions but not necessarily optimal ones.
quotes: This is likely due to the warmstarts finding relatively high cost solutions, but not necessarily optimal ones.

assertions.value: The authors report that the vertex-at-top rotation choices rank, in decreasing performance for all problems except TSP, as last, first, and no rotation.
quotes: the vertex on top rotation choices ranked in order of decreasing performance (for all problems except TSP) are last, first, and no rotation.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in general, QUBO-Relaxed with 50 initializations slightly outperforms QUBO-Relaxed with 10 initializations.
quotes: In general, QUBO-Relaxed with 50 initializations slightly outperforms QUBO-Relaxed with 10 initializations.
Empirically we saw that 50 initializations generally outperformed 10 initializations, but this difference was problem dependent.

assertions.value: The authors state that for portfolio optimization the QUBO relaxation can be solved directly, so the number of random initializations does not matter.
quotes: Portfolio Optimization is actually a QUBO-Relaxed problem when relaxed, so we can solve for
Thus, the number of random initializations does not matter for Portfolio Optimization.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer printed the word convex as QUBO-Relaxed throughout; the surrounding argument (negative semidefinite matrix) shows the intended word is convex.

assertions.value: The authors report that the difference in optimal sampling probability between 50 and 10 initializations is largest for TSP and the MIS problems, both of which arise from constrained optimization problems.
quotes: the difference in obtained optimal sampling probability between 50 and 10 initializations is largest for TSP and the MIS problems, both of which arise from constrained optimization problems.

assertions.value: The authors suggest that constrained optimization problems are intrinsically more difficult to solve and that this structural difference is preserved when the problems are mapped to QAOA.
quotes: This suggests that constrained optimization problems are intrinsically more difficult to solve, and this structural difference is preserved when these problems are mapped to QAOA.

assertions.value: The authors report that for both random QUBO types GW2 outperforms QUBO-Relaxed with both 50 and 10 initializations on instance-specific approximation ratio, while QUBO-Relaxed with 10 initializations outperforms GW2 on optimal sampling probability.
quotes: GW2 outperforms QUBO-Relaxed with both 50 and 10 initializations
QUBO-Relaxed with 10 initializations outperforms GW2 in both instances

assertions.value: The authors state that the difference between the two metrics for random QUBOs is likely due to GW2 creating initial states that are superpositions of the optimal state and other high-cost but suboptimal states.
quotes: The difference between these metrics is likely due to GW2 creating initial states that are superpositions of the optimal state and other high-cost but suboptimal states

assertions.value: The authors state that for their TSP case of 5 cities there are 216 possible QUBO bitstrings (as printed) but only 24 feasible solutions.
quotes: For our case of 5 cities, there are 216 possible QUBO bitstrings but only 24 feasible solutions.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer likely printed 2 to the power 16 flat as 216; the TSP QUBO has 16 variables (Sec. 3.3).

assertions.value: The authors report that for TSP optimal sampling probability the warmstarts rank, in decreasing order, GW2 no rotation, QUBO-Relaxed with 10 initializations, QUBO-Relaxed with 50, and none are within 0.25 standard deviations of each other.
quotes: the warmstarts in decreasing order are, GW2 no rotation, QUBO-Relaxed with 10 initializations, QUBO-Relaxed with 50.
None of these are within 0.25 standard deviations of each other.

assertions.value: The authors state that QUBO-Relaxed performing better with fewer initializations on TSP is surprising and likely an artifact of the generally low optimal sampling probabilities.
quotes: Although QUBO-Relaxed performing better with fewer initializations is surprising, it is likely an artifact of the generally low optimal sampling probabilities.

assertions.value: The authors report that for portfolio optimization both metrics fall under the category where GW2 outperforms QUBO-Relaxed.
quotes: both metrics fall under (↑) with GW2 outperforming QUBO-Relaxed.

assertions.value: The authors report that for both MIS problems and both metrics the order is QUBO-Relaxed with 50 initializations, GW2 Last rotation, then QUBO-Relaxed with 10 initializations.
quotes: Both MIS problems considering both metrics fall under (↔), specifically following the order of QUBO-Relaxed with 50 initializations, GW2 Last rotation, then QUBO-Relaxed with 10 initializations.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that the best SDP warmstart was Goemans-Williamson projected onto 2 dimensions, with a rotation applied to the auxiliary variable introduced in the mapping from QUBOs to Max-Cuts.
quotes: We found that the best choice of SDP warmstart was Goemans-Williamson projected onto 2 dimensions, with a rotation applied to the auxiliary variable introduced in the mapping from QUBOs to Max-Cuts.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper also finds the relative performance is problem and metric dependent, so this conclusion is not general.

assertions.value: The authors state that, because the non-convex-type optimization has no performance guarantees, they expect larger problems to need more iterations.
quotes: we expect that for larger problems, more iterations would be needed.

assertions.value: The authors state that the relative performance of GW2 warmstarts and QUBO-Relaxed is problem and metric dependent, and that the mechanisms behind these differences remain to be better understood.
quotes: The relative performance of QAOA between GW2 warmstarts and QUBO-Relaxed is problem and metric dependent.
Future researchers might be interested in better understanding the mechanisms behind these differences.
